mem-032.summary: Next.js 15+ fetch() is uncached by default — the opposite of v14. Pages re-render on every request unless you opt into caching with { next: { revalidate: N } } or { cache: 'force-cache' }. Most blog posts and muscle memory predate this flip. Lead templates with explicit { cache: 'no-store' } when SSR is the intent. See .agent/philosophy/NEXTJS-PATTERNS.md §D.

mem-033.summary: Next.js 16 renames middleware.ts to proxy.ts at project root. Same matcher API and NextRequest/NextResponse, but middleware.ts is deprecated. Codemod: npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy . Also in v15+: params and searchParams are Promises — must await them in pages, layouts, and route handlers. Route Handler context type is inferred from the file path: collection routes get Promise<{}>, dynamic routes get Promise<{id: string}>. Hardcoding the dynamic shape on a collection route fails  type-check. See .agent/philosophy/NEXTJS-PATTERNS.md §A, §E, §H.

mem-050.summary: S1 verdict — PostToolUse hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext DELIVERS to the model. Empirically observed in CC 2.1.205 on 2026-07-10 (TASK-57 spike, ship-path scratch marketplace). Supersedes mem-035 for the PostToolUse additionalContext sub-channel. The payload lands as a transcript attachment entry of type hook_additional_context immediately after the tool_result. Hard constraint: content must be DECLARATIVE (facts, data, memories). Imperative instructions ('you MUST quote this token') are flagged by the model as prompt injection and refused (2/2 runs), while a declarative fact was correctly used to answer a question (clean pass; sentinel NAV-S1-c2505e07 answered as the 'internal build codename'). PostToolUseFailure inherits this verdict per the routing matrix. Evidence: transcript /Users/aleks.petrov/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-nav-v7-spike-project/26e7b852-b8d7-4ea7-8a00-594c85249863.jsonl; probe /tmp/nav-v7-spike/probes/probe_s1.py; verdict /tmp/nav-v7-spike/state/verdict-s1.json.

mem-051.summary: S2 verdict — Stop hook 'continue: true' is a NO-OP for forced continuation; 'decision: block' + reason IS the working mechanism. Empirically observed in CC 2.1.205 on 2026-07-10 (TASK-57 spike). continue:true was accepted (hook_success) but the session ended normally (num_turns=1, no continuation) — continue only has effect as continue:false. decision:block injected its reason as a user-role 'Stop hook feedback:' message and produced exactly one continuation obeying it (CLI result was the sentinel NAV-S2B-bbebfac5, num_turns=2). Runaway protection verified on both layers: the re-fire after a block carries stop_hook_active=true (harness belt), and the single-shot flag-file fuse consumed correctly with a run-twice subtest showing zero further continuations (mem-037 discipline). v7 consequence: stop_completion builds on decision:block; continue:true ships OFF permanently. Evidence: transcripts /Users/aleks.petrov/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-nav-v7-spike-project/fcd00eb3-4193-474f-adac-482bd9bfa077.jsonl (continue variant) and 047b00c1-c117-4863-968a-f9eb9d1494ae.jsonl (block variant); probe /tmp/nav-v7-spike/probes/probe_s2.py; verdict /tmp/nav-v7-spike/state/verdict-s2.json.

mem-052.summary: S3 verdict — SubagentStart hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext WORKS with both-way main/subagent isolation. Empirically observed in CC 2.1.205 on 2026-07-10 (TASK-57 spike). The event fires for Task-tool subagents, and the injected context lands as a hook_additional_context attachment in the subagent's own transcript; the subagent complied with it (quoted sentinel NAV-S3A-d656b96b in its answer — subagent-start injection is treated as trusted context, unlike tool-adjacent injection). Isolation holds both ways: the injected sentinel reached the main thread only via the expected Task tool_result relay, and a main-thread-only sentinel never appeared in the subagent transcript. Harness facts: subagent transcripts are SEPARATE files at <session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl under the project slug dir (not sidechain entries in the main JSONL); hook payload carries agent_type. v7 consequence: subagent_context feature is viable at the 2k-char budget. Evidence: transcripts /Users/aleks.petrov/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-nav-v7-spike-project/670f5507-8980-4174-99e7-ac7f83c4314f.jsonl and its subagents/agent-afbe4a5fb40770c7f.jsonl; probe /tmp/nav-v7-spike/probes/probe_s3.py; verdict /tmp/nav-v7-spike/state/verdict-s3.json.

mem-053.summary: S4 verdict — UserPromptSubmit block-as-answer WORKS with zero model invocation; WINNER: decision:block JSON (over exit-2 stderr). Empirically observed in CC 2.1.205 on 2026-07-10 (TASK-57 spike). Both variants blocked the trigger turn with num_turns=0, duration_api_ms=0, all-zero usage and modelUsage={} — a genuinely zero-token deterministic answer path for Tier-1. Rendering: decision:block shows 'UserPromptSubmit operation blocked by hook:' plus the reason (clean); exit-2 leaks the raw hook command chrome into the visible answer. Echo hygiene (mem-034): the same-session follow-up prompt passed through without re-trigger and answered normally with no block-text leakage; caution — Claude Code itself appends 'Original prompt: <trigger>' to the block message, so the trigger phrase re-enters the transcript regardless of hook-side hygiene; transcript/context-scanning hooks must tolerate that echo. Scripting note: a blocked turn still returns subtype success, exit 0 — detect blocks via num_turns==0 or the result prefix, never exit codes. Evidence: transcripts /Users/aleks.petrov/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-nav-v7-spike-project/69c208c3-55b4-4c9b-b607-142af26fddfe.jsonl (decision:block) and 58150d0e-5aa9-4afd-a9b1-76d86accbcc9.jsonl (exit-2); probe /tmp/nav-v7-spike/probes/probe_s4.py; verdict /tmp/nav-v7-spike/state/verdict-s4.json.

mem-054.summary: S5 verdict — PreToolUse split result: plain stdout is DEAD (reconfirms mem-035 for stdout); hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext DELIVERS (SUPERSEDES mem-035 for that sub-channel). Empirically observed in CC 2.1.205 on 2026-07-10 (TASK-57 spike), reproduced across clean runs. Stdout variant: sentinel appears only in a hook_success transcript attachment (hook-output logging, not model-visible); the model explicitly answered 'no codename' — clean negative. Context variant: sentinel lands as a hook_additional_context attachment and the model answered the codename question with it (NAV-S5C-b307f7bf). Same declarative-only constraint as S1: imperative instructions via tool-adjacent additionalContext are flagged as prompt injection and refused. Docs remain untrustworthy for this class of behavior — only version-stamped empirical results count; per plan, read_guard stays deny-only regardless (advisory redesign is a v7.x follow-up, not TASK-61). Evidence: transcripts /Users/aleks.petrov/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-nav-v7-spike-project/83ed067c-dd03-479e-8db5-dc111345c3b9.jsonl (stdout) and e0cee530-2e10-457f-8e89-b39330035ea7.jsonl (context); probe /tmp/nav-v7-spike/probes/probe_s5.py; verdict /tmp/nav-v7-spike/state/verdict-s5.json.

mem-055.summary: S6 verdict — ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} binds correctly in plugin-manifest hook commands, including headless claude -p sessions. Empirically observed in CC 2.1.205 on 2026-07-10 (TASK-57 spike). For directory-source marketplaces it binds to the marketplace SOURCE path (/tmp/nav-v7-spike/marketplace/nav-spike), not the ~/.claude/plugins/cache copy — source edits take effect in new sessions without reinstall. Unset/empty env is a LOUD failure (exit 2, python cannot open /hooks/...), not mem-036's silent no-op — the :-fallback pattern stays prudent for commands that might run outside plugin context. SessionStart DOES fire in headless -p sessions. Two conformance-relevant harness facts: hooks that print no stdout leave NO transcript attachment (silent hooks are transcript-invisible; suites need side-channel logs), and hook payload cwd arrives realpath'd on macOS (/tmp becomes /private/tmp) while $PWD may stay logical — never gate hooks on raw string-prefix cwd checks; resolve paths first. mem-080.summary: Mods: $.state survives hot reload, so a changed value shape (new field) reaches the new module as the OLD object; a ui.render that dereferences the new field throws, the engine skips the hook and the pane renders empty. Read state through helpers that merge stored values over defaults. The test kit cannot seed stale state: $ has no state noun and state.get is not interceptable by a prepend inline plugin.
